learning_design.unlock_rule: Reveal the required explanations and required code annotations to unlock each knowledge node.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery builds the model first; quiz attempts provide the scored retrieval and application evidence.

authoring_notes: Targets Terraform Associate 004 / Terraform 1.12. Domain weight 0.125 is an internal planning weight because HashiCorp does not publish objective percentages. This v2 learning content uses real tables and interactive syntax-highlighted code_file reveals; generic exam-clue and generic mental-model prompts were intentionally removed.

prompts.label: COMPARE BLOCK TYPES
prompts.placeholder: The two blocks can look similar, but their ownership intent is different. Click each block keyword.

annotations.title: Managed resource
annotations.explanation: A resource block asks Terraform to manage the lifecycle of a remote object through create/read/update/delete behavior.

annotations.title: Data source
annotations.explanation: A data block reads information that exists elsewhere. It does not claim lifecycle ownership of that object.

prompts.label: OWNERSHIP DIFFERENCE
prompts.placeholder: What is the practical difference between resource and data?

nodes.title: References pass values and create graph edges

prompts.label: FOLLOW THE REFERENCE
prompts.placeholder: This subnet needs the ID produced by another resource. Click the reference and see why Terraform already knows the dependency.

annotations.title: Cross-resource reference
annotations.explanation: This expression reads the id attribute from aws_vpc.main. Because the value is needed by the subnet, Terraform can infer that the VPC operation must happen first.

prompts.label: DO NOT ADD depends_on BY HABIT
prompts.placeholder: If a normal expression reference already represents the real dependency, should you also add depends_on?

reveal.text: Usually no. Prefer data references because they express both the value flow and the dependency. Use explicit depends_on only for a real hidden dependency that cannot be expressed through data.

nodes.title: Input variables are the module interface

prompts.label: INSPECT variables.tf
prompts.placeholder: Variables accept values from callers instead of hard-coding every environment-specific setting. Click the declaration parts.

annotations.title: Input variable declaration
annotations.explanation: The block declares an input named environment. Code inside the module references it as var.environment.

annotations.title: Type constraint
annotations.explanation: A type constraint catches incompatible caller values and documents the expected shape.

annotations.title: Fallback value
annotations.explanation: A default makes the variable optional for callers. Supplied variable values override the declaration default.

annotations.title: Complex collection type
annotations.explanation: Terraform type constraints can describe collections and structural values, not only primitive strings and numbers.

prompts.label: VALUE SOURCES
prompts.placeholder: Which common value sources can replace a variable declaration default?

cells.effect: Fallback when no higher-precedence value is supplied
Can supply a value that overrides the default
Can supply a value that overrides the default
Explicitly supplies a value and overrides the default

prompts.label: INSPECT outputs.tf
prompts.placeholder: An output is an explicit value leaving a module. Click the name and value expression.

annotations.title: Named output
annotations.explanation: A child module output becomes part of that module’s public interface. The root module also uses outputs to present selected values after runs.

annotations.title: Output expression
annotations.explanation: The output evaluates an expression and exposes its result. Child-module callers can reference it as module.<name>.vpc_id.

prompts.label: INPUTS VS OUTPUTS
prompts.placeholder: Which direction does data cross a module boundary?

nodes.title: Choose types that match the data shape

prompts.label: COMMON TYPE SHAPES
prompts.placeholder: Which Terraform type fits each kind of configuration value?

cells.shape: Ordered values of one element type
Unique unordered values of one element type
String keys to one element type
Named attributes with their own types
Fixed positions with independently typed elements

prompts.label: TERRAFORM CAN CONVERT SOME VALUES
prompts.placeholder: Why still declare an explicit variable type if Terraform can perform some automatic conversions?

reveal.text: Type constraints document the expected interface and reject incompatible shapes early. Automatic conversion is useful, but it should not replace a clear contract.

prompts.label: READ THE DATA TRANSFORMS
prompts.placeholder: Terraform expressions combine references, operators, and functions. Click the examples to see what each transformation does.

annotations.title: Function call on a referenced value
annotations.explanation: lower transforms the input string; expressions can derive values instead of requiring every value to be supplied directly.

annotations.title: Combine maps/objects
annotations.explanation: merge combines maps or objects; later arguments win when keys overlap.

annotations.title: Fallback across expressions
annotations.explanation: try evaluates expressions in order and returns the first one that does not produce an error.

prompts.label: FUNCTION INTENT
prompts.placeholder: Match useful functions to the problem they solve.

cells.purpose: Return the first expression that does not error

nodes.title: count and for_each create multiple instances

prompts.label: INDEX VS STABLE KEY
prompts.placeholder: When should you prefer count versus for_each?

cells.good_fit: Simple N copies or list positions where index identity is acceptable
cells.watch_out: Removing/reordering list elements can shift indexes
Keys must be known before apply

prompts.label: INSPECT for_each
prompts.placeholder: This map uses stable service names as instance keys. Click for_each and each.key.

annotations.title: Create one instance per key
annotations.explanation: for_each creates instances keyed by map keys or set members, which makes addresses stable and meaningful.

annotations.title: Current instance key
annotations.explanation: Inside a for_each block, each.key identifies the current map/set key.

annotations.title: Current map value
annotations.explanation: For a map, each.value is the value associated with the current key.

nodes.title: Terraform can read and write YAML documents

prompts.label: FIRST: THE YAML FILE
prompts.placeholder: Terraform configuration is normally HCL in .tf files. This is an external YAML data file that Terraform will read.

reveal.code:
application:
  name: checkout
  replicas: 3
  regions:
    - us-east-1
    - us-west-2

annotations.title: YAML mapping
annotations.explanation: This is YAML data, not Terraform configuration. Terraform can parse it into Terraform values with yamldecode.

annotations.title: YAML scalar value
annotations.explanation: After yamldecode, this number becomes accessible through the resulting Terraform object.

annotations.title: YAML list field
annotations.explanation: The nested YAML list is decoded into a Terraform collection value.

prompts.label: THEN: THE TERRAFORM FILE
prompts.placeholder: Now inspect the HCL that loads config.yaml. Click the file() read and yamldecode() parse steps.

annotations.title: Read the file as text
annotations.explanation: file reads the YAML document contents from disk.

annotations.title: Parse YAML into Terraform values
annotations.explanation: yamldecode converts a YAML string into the corresponding Terraform value structure.

annotations.title: Use the decoded value
annotations.explanation: After decoding, normal Terraform expressions can navigate the resulting object and collections.

nodes.title: Use depends_on only for hidden dependencies

prompts.label: IMPLICIT FIRST, EXPLICIT WHEN NEEDED
prompts.placeholder: How should you express a dependency?

cells.case: Downstream argument uses an upstream attribute
cells.best_model: Use the expression reference; Terraform infers the dependency

cells.case: Downstream behavior depends on an upstream object but consumes none of its data
cells.best_model: Use depends_on to model the hidden dependency

cells.case: You only want a specific file order
cells.best_model: Do not use file order; Terraform uses the dependency graph

prompts.label: HIDDEN DEPENDENCY EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: This policy attachment must exist before a data read, but the data block does not consume one of its values. Click depends_on.

annotations.title: Explicit hidden dependency
annotations.explanation: depends_on tells Terraform to finish operations on the referenced object before this block is evaluated. Use it when normal data references cannot express the real dependency.

nodes.title: Lifecycle rules change replacement and update behavior

prompts.label: LIFECYCLE RULES
prompts.placeholder: Which lifecycle rule solves which problem?

cells.effect: Create the replacement before destroying the old object
cells.caution: May fail when the remote system requires a globally unique name

cells.effect: Reject plans that would destroy the configured resource
cells.caution: Removing the entire resource block also removes this protection

cells.effect: Ignore selected remote changes when planning updates
cells.caution: Can hide intentional drift if overused

cells.effect: Replace when referenced managed resources/attributes change
cells.caution: Tracks managed resource changes, not arbitrary plain values directly

prompts.label: INSPECT lifecycle
prompts.placeholder: This resource wants replacement before destruction and refuses ordinary destroy plans. Click both rules.

annotations.title: Reverse replacement order
annotations.explanation: Terraform normally destroys then creates when replacement is required. create_before_destroy asks it to create the replacement first.

annotations.title: Reject destructive plans
annotations.explanation: prevent_destroy causes Terraform to reject a plan that would destroy this configured resource. It is a guardrail, not a backup system.

nodes.title: Custom conditions validate at different stages

prompts.label: CUSTOM CONDITION TYPES
prompts.placeholder: Where should a condition live based on what you are validating?

cells.use: Reject invalid input values at the variable boundary
Assert something must be true before a resource/data/output operation proceeds
Assert something about a result after evaluation/apply
Continuously validate broader infrastructure assertions without blocking every operation in the same way as resource conditions

prompts.label: VARIABLE VALIDATION EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: This variable accepts CIDR text only when cidrnetmask can parse it. Click validation, can(), and error_message.

annotations.title: Variable boundary check
annotations.explanation: A validation block rejects caller input that does not satisfy its condition.

annotations.title: Convert parse failure into false
annotations.explanation: can returns false instead of propagating an expression error, which makes it useful for validation of parsable formats.

anchor.text: error_message = "cidr must use valid CIDR notation"

annotations.title: Actionable failure message
annotations.explanation: The message should tell the caller what is wrong and what shape of value is expected.

nodes.title: Sensitive is about display, not persistence

prompts.label: DISPLAY VS PERSISTENCE
prompts.placeholder: These features solve different secret-handling problems. Which one does what?

cells.state_plan: Omitted from Terraform plan/state where supported
cells.purpose: Keep temporary values out of Terraform artifacts

cells.state_plan: Value is not persisted by Terraform in the normal readable attribute
cells.purpose: Pass a temporary secret into a provider-managed operation

prompts.label: REDACTED DOES NOT MEAN ABSENT
prompts.placeholder: If a value is marked sensitive, can you assume it is absent from state?

reveal.text: No. sensitive primarily controls presentation. Protect state storage, and use ephemeral/write-only flows when you specifically need a value omitted from Terraform artifacts.

nodes.title: Ephemeral values stay out of plan/state

prompts.label: INSPECT EPHEMERAL VALUES
prompts.placeholder: These values are meant to exist during an operation without being retained in normal Terraform artifacts. Click the ephemeral pieces.

annotations.title: Hide normal display
annotations.explanation: Sensitive redacts the value in normal output, but redaction alone does not guarantee non-persistence.

annotations.title: Ephemeral input variable
annotations.explanation: An ephemeral variable is available during the operation but omitted from plan and state artifacts.

annotations.title: Ephemeral resource block
annotations.explanation: An ephemeral block can obtain or generate temporary data for the operation without persisting the resulting value to state.

prompts.label: PASSING THE VALUE TO A RESOURCE
prompts.placeholder: How can an ephemeral secret be consumed by a managed resource without turning it back into a persisted readable value?

reveal.text: Use a provider-supported write-only argument. Terraform passes the value to the provider during the operation but does not store that write-only value as a normal readable attribute.

nodes.title: Vault is a secret source, not a persistence guarantee

prompts.label: SECRET FLOW
prompts.placeholder: Where does Vault fit in Terraform secret handling?

items: Vault centrally stores or dynamically issues a secret
Terraform/provider retrieves the secret for a run
Terraform configuration passes the value to the target operation
Terraform persistence semantics still depend on whether the consuming path is normal, sensitive, ephemeral, or write-only

prompts.label: SOURCE VS STORAGE
prompts.placeholder: What problem does each layer solve?

cells.solves: Secret issuance, central management, leasing/rotation depending on secret engine
Avoid persistence in Terraform artifacts where the flow supports it
Protect state that legitimately contains sensitive values
